title: Local Hilbert--Samuel presentations and their admissible transforms
statement:
Let $X$ be a reduced scheme of finite type over $\mathbf Q$, locally closed embedded in a smooth scheme $Z$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $h_x(n)=\operatorname{length}(\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x^{n+1})$, where length is composition length [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Write $\Lambda f(n)=\sum_{i=0}^n f(i)$ and $H_x=\Lambda^{\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbf Q}\kappa(x)}h_x$. The function $H$ has finite image locally on $X$, is upper semicontinuous in lexicographic order, cannot increase under a blowup along a smooth $H$-constant center, and admits no infinite strictly decreasing sequence of values arising under these admissible blowups of an initial finite-dimensional $X$.

At each point there is, after restriction and an etale neighbourhood [def-weil-etale-morphism], a presentation of $H$: a smooth $N\hookrightarrow Z$, coherent ideal $I\subset\mathcal O_N$ and positive integer $b$, whose cosupport is $\{x:\operatorname{ord}_x I\ge b\}$. Here order is the supremum of the $r$ with $I_x\subset\mathfrak m_x^r$, allowing $+\infty$ for the zero ideal. A presentation has the same admissible test sequences as the corresponding $H$-stratum: a test sequence consists of smooth blowups in the indicated stratum transverse to the ordered exceptional divisors, products with an affine line, and blowups of intersections of two exceptional divisors; $X$ transforms by scheme-theoretic strict transform, and $I$ by total transform divided by the $b$th power of the new exceptional ideal for an admissible blowup. Transverse means that center and divisor equations are subsets of one etale coordinate system; exceptional divisors locally have equation a product of distinct coordinate parameters. For the other two test operations use ordinary pullback of $I$. Two presentations are equivalent when their test sequences coincide.

A presentation can be made of maximal order (order $b$ throughout its cosupport) and codimension zero ($N=Z$), using a minimal smooth local embedding of $X$. The resulting equivalence class, including transforms and ordered exceptional data, depends only on the strict-transform scheme and its ordered earlier center ideals, is independent of the chosen minimal embedding, and commutes with restriction and smooth pullback. Resolving the presentation of a maximum $H$-stratum makes that maximum disappear. These assertions hold successively along admissible histories [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-strict-transform]; they concern presentations, not a completed resolution tower.
